findings.title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched in this test
findings.body: test_basic does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at module-attribute level, so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` (with the comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") does not sleep at all — it calls the patched lambda. The intended delay to let the flusher thread observe the drift change before `step.join()` sets `stopped=True` never happens, so the test relies on the busy-spinning thread happening to flush in time and can be flaky. Note test_flusher.py avoids this because it does `from time import sleep`, which still references the real function. Use the same import pattern (or patch differently) so the delay is real.

findings.title: New multiprocess test only checks bookkeeping, not flush correctness
findings.body: test_flusher_processes_limit asserts `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `max_processes == 2`, `num_processes == 2`, and that the shard count sums to 4. It never writes spans to the shared-process shards and verifies that exactly the expected segments are flushed to the produce pipe (and not duplicated or dropped). Since the whole point of this PR is to safely shard flushing across processes, a regression where a shard is never flushed, or two processes flush the same shard, would still pass this test. Add an end-to-end assertion on produced output for the multi-process/shared-shard case.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key ("shards" vs "shard") on wait_produce timer
findings.body: The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer now uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` while the sibling metrics `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`. The label name is different, so dashboards/alerts that slice by `shard` across these metrics will silently omit wait_produce. Use the same key (`shard`) for all three.

findings.title: Class docstring claims one process per shard, but default creates a single process for all shards
findings.body: The docstring says "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing", but `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` and `max_processes` defaults to 1 (both in the click option default and via `max_processes or len(...)` when None). With the default, all shards are handled by a single process, and even when `max_processes < num_shards` multiple shards share a process. The docstring misdescribes the actual behavior and should state that shards are distributed across up to `max_processes` flusher processes.

findings.title: join() timeouts leave remaining flusher processes un-terminated; remaining_time is unused
findings.body: In `join()`, when the deadline elapses (`remaining_time <= 0`) the loop `break`s, so the remaining child processes in `self.processes` are neither waited on nor `terminate()`d — only the ones iterated before the break are terminated. Additionally `remaining_time` is computed but never used. On a bounded-timeout shutdown/rebalance this can leave flusher processes running past the deadline (relying on daemon-kill at parent exit), which could keep producing segments concurrently with a new assignment. Terminate/join the remaining processes after the loop (or handle them explicitly) instead of breaking out silently.
